title: Validate Nodes Form One Binary Tree
statement:
You are given an array of `n` node records. Each record has a unique integer `id` and the ids of its `left` and `right` children, where `-1` means the child is absent. A child id refers to another node by id; it may or may not belong to the array.

Decide whether the records describe **exactly one binary tree that uses every node of the array**. This holds when all of the following are true:

- Every child id that is not `-1` is the id of some node **in the array** (the tree must not reach a node that is missing from the array).
- Every node is the child of **at most one** node, counting both child slots (so a node cannot be both the left and right child of the same parent, and a node cannot be its own child).
- There is exactly one node that is nobody's child: the root.
- Starting from the root and following child links reaches **all** `n` nodes (no node is left out in a separate component, and there are no cycles).

Print `true` if the array describes a single valid binary tree and `false` otherwise. The records can appear in any order.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
Each of the next `n` lines contains three integers `id`, `left`, `right`: the node's id and the ids of its left and right children (`-1` for none).
outputFormat: Print `true` if the nodes form exactly one binary tree containing all of them, otherwise `false`.
constraints: 0 ≤ id ≤ 10^9, and all ids in the array are distinct
each child value is -1 or an integer between 0 and 10^9 + 10 (it may name a node that is not in the array)
every simple path that follows child links contains at most 5000 nodes

examples.explanation: Node 10 is nobody's child, so it is the root. Following child links from it reaches 20, 30 and 40, so all four nodes belong to one tree.
Node 3 points to a child with id 9, which is not in the array, so the tree contains a node that is missing from it.
Every node is somebody's child (the links form a cycle), so there is no root.

hints: Count how many parents each node has. What must be true of the number of nodes with no parent, and of every node's parent count, in a tree?
Look up child ids in a hash map built from the array. A child id that is not in the map means the tree escapes the array.
Having one root and no node with two parents is not enough, because a separate cycle can hide elsewhere. Traverse from the root and check that you visit all n nodes.
